newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador to probe oil corruption charges.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador to probe oil corruption charges.

text.p: The president of Ecuador's state oil company Petroecuador, Rafael Almeida, said Monday he will investigate recent oil contracts for signs of corruption.

"We have requested our investigative units...to audit all procedures in which there is suspicion of corruption," Almeida told a local television channel. "Our different branches have signed a series of contracts and it seems there have been irregular procedures."
President Fabian Alarcon's government has denounced corruption in the oil industry during the former administration of Abdala Bucaram, who was sacked in February on grounds of "mental incompetence."
Petroecuador produces more than 80 percent of Ecuador's hydrocarbon output of 390,000 barrels per day.
Almeida also said the expansion of the Trans-Ecuadorean oil pipeline could be completed within eight months if international companies take part in the $80 million project.
Petroecuador called a tender Saturday for companies to join the project to boost the pipeline's carrying capacity to 410,000 bpd from 300,000 bpd.
"If Petroecuador does it itself, the project would take approximately 10 months. If companies able to boost production participate, it could be shortened to eight months," Almeida said.
Ecuador is the third biggest oil exporter in Latin America after Mexico and Venezuela, and finances 50 percent of its budget through sales of crude oil.
